decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY establishing revised-script precedence for SQ12 shot angles; no additional update or removal is required.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording the revised script as authoritative and conflicting storyboard angles as incorrect.
The existing same-message MODIFY already records script authority over conflicting storyboard angles, with no stale attribute requiring removal.
The prior unconditional permission to change shot angles for image quality must be qualified where the revised script explicitly prescribes the required angle over an incorrect storyboard angle.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The script already specified the shot angles I wanted and explicitly noted that the storyboard angles were wrong. If you followed only the storyboard reel rather than the script, that explains why we misunderstood each other. Since I can’t reliably create images with the right angles to demonstrate them in the reel, what alternative process would work for you? How should I communicate each angle so you can render the shot correctly?

value_updates.shot_angle_adjustment_for_quality: Shot angles may be changed to improve set-image quality except where the revised script explicitly identifies the storyboard angle as wrong and specifies the required angle.

decisions.reason: Shot-angle source precedence does not change responsibility for producing text cards.
The requirement that sets remain visually distinct is independent of whether revised-script or storyboard shot angles control.
The source does not identify the character-pair framing progression as conflicting with the revised script or otherwise alter its specified framing order.
The source establishes angle-source precedence but does not change the existence, position, or deferred status of the opening aerial shot.
Revised-script angle precedence does not alter the requirement for stylistic continuity across set imagery.
The bridge-removal and retained-bridge composition rules are unaffected by the decision about script versus storyboard shot angles.
